comparison: Perfect alignment on claims C40-C43 regarding stress effects being specific to decision-making rather than motor performance. Both evaluations support these null findings and their interpretation that stress affected motivation rather than ability.

Strong alignment on stress manipulation effectiveness (C31-C34). OpenEval explicitly evaluates the statistical evidence for stress induction, while peer reviewers implicitly accepted the manipulation as 'established' and 'solid' without raising concerns.

Strong agreement on the main behavioral finding (C4, C35-C39, C64, C68) showing stress reduced prosocial effort. Both evaluations support this as a major result with appropriate statistical analysis. Peer review also includes broader interpretive claims (C64, C68, C101) that OpenEval addresses separately.

Strong alignment on neural individual differences (C58-C62). Both support the finding that SVO moderates stress effects in dACC. Peer review also includes C89 and C91, which OpenEval addresses in R13, showing some overlap in how individual difference neural findings are grouped.

Substantial overlap on dACC/AI findings (C50-C53). OpenEval notes the absence of Group × Recipient interaction as a limitation, while peer reviewers endorsed the findings as 'sophisticated' and 'informative' without raising this concern. Peer review also includes broader interpretive claims (C6, C65, C103).

Both address brain-behavior correlations (C55-C56). OpenEval explicitly evaluates the dACC correlation and null AI finding, while peer reviewers implicitly supported these mechanistic links as part of broader neural findings without specific discussion.

Both address computational modeling approach (C124). OpenEval provides detailed evaluation of model comparison procedures, while peer reviewers praised the modeling as 'sophisticated' without specific methodological concerns.

Substantial overlap on individual differences in behavior (C45-C48). OpenEval notes heterogeneity within groups as a nuance, while peer reviewers endorsed this as a major finding. Peer review also includes C5, C66, and C83, showing broader grouping of individual difference claims.

Both address dlPFC findings (C76). OpenEval notes the speculative nature since dlPFC was not an a priori ROI, while peer reviewers accepted the whole-brain findings without raising concerns about post-hoc interpretation.

Minimal overlap on baseline equivalence (C44). OpenEval includes this as part of the individual differences analysis, while peer reviewers treat it as a separate methodological validation supporting randomization.

Minimal overlap on cortisol findings (C54). OpenEval addresses the absence of Group × Recipient interaction in perceived stress, while peer reviewers address null cortisol-behavior relationships more broadly (C49, C54).

Partial overlap on neural individual differences (C89, C91). OpenEval groups these with broader contextualization claims (C87-C95), while peer reviewers group them with other SVO × stress neural findings (C58-C62).
Partial overlap on main conclusions (C64, C68). OpenEval synthesizes these as part of broader findings summary, while peer reviewers include them with the primary behavioral results (C4, C35-C39).
OpenEval identifies claims C69-C70 as speculative interpretations requiring additional testing. Peer reviewers did not explicitly address these reconciliation attempts with prior literature.

OpenEval evaluates claims C71-C73 about dACC function and psychological processes. Peer reviewers did not explicitly discuss these theoretical interpretations, though they endorsed the broader neural findings.

OpenEval evaluates claims C81-C86 about reduced flexibility and automatic responding. Peer reviewers did not explicitly address these interpretive claims, though C83 appears in their individual differences evaluation (R3).
OpenEval evaluates methodological limitations (C96-C97, C105-C106) including male-only sample and power calculations. Peer reviewers did not explicitly discuss these limitations in their evaluation.

OpenEval evaluates detailed methodological procedures (C107-C122) including exclusion criteria, stress protocol, and task design. Peer reviewers endorsed the overall approach as 'solid' without evaluating specific procedural claims.
OpenEval evaluates neuroimaging acquisition and preprocessing methods (C125-C128). Peer reviewers did not explicitly address these technical methodological details.
OpenEval evaluates literature review claims (C1-C3, C7-C15) about mixed findings and study motivation. Peer reviewers did not explicitly evaluate these background claims.
OpenEval evaluates theoretical framework claims (C16-C24) from prior research on stress, effort, and neural mechanisms. Peer reviewers did not explicitly evaluate these foundational claims.
OpenEval evaluates rationale for individual differences analysis (C25-C29). Peer reviewers endorsed the individual differences findings but did not explicitly evaluate the theoretical rationale.

OpenEval evaluates summary conclusions and implications (C98-C104). Peer reviewers acknowledged the findings would be 'of interest' but did not explicitly evaluate these broader interpretive claims, though C101 and C103 appear in their behavioral and neural evaluations.
